sliceReports.summary: Made SidekickMenu search opt-in for v2.0.0. UI/SidekickMenu/SidekickMenu.tsx: searchEnabled now defaults to false (the existing `searchEnabled && !effectiveRailCollapsed` guard unmounts the input entirely, so nothing invisible is focusable, and the null-guarded autofocus effect no-ops). Added a small effect that dispatches SET_SEARCH_TERM "" when search is turned off while a term is active, so the menu is never left filtered by an invisible query. Search enabled keeps every 1.7.0 path unchanged (placeholder, autofocus, icon, matching, ordering, numbered shortcuts, empty list). types.ts documents searchEnabled as opt-in with default false. Updated every existing search test to pass searchEnabled (none deleted or skipped) and added tests for the hidden default, false/undefined, opt-in rendering, prop-flip term reset, autofocus, rail collapse, no-match empty state, non-persistence, plus release metadata. Bumped package.json to 2.0.0, added the v2.0.0 breaking-changes entry with the searchEnabled={true} migration and ToC item, and updated README/docs/features/docs/examples to present search as opt-in. docs/api.md and docs/configuration.md were intentionally left to the other build slice (out of this step's declared parts) and remain in the repo's pre-existing state for that step. Build passes. Focused suite: 55/55. Full suite: 211 passed, 2 failed in Styles/SidekickMenu.theme.test.ts only - both are pre-existing Windows/CRLF regex failures in an untouched file (the working-tree Styles/SidekickMenu.module.css is CRLF while those tests read it expecting LF), unrelated to this change.

findings.description: The performance non-functional requirement is unmet and unproven: both bundles are measurably larger than v1.7.0's, and the MenuButton helper added at lines 42-43 (used by the hamburger and rail toggle, unrelated to this feature) is pure avoidable payload. The developer's report claims 'no bundle growth', which the measurement contradicts.
findings.evidence: I rebuilt both revisions in scratch copies with the project's own rollup.config.js and a junction to the same node_modules. v1.7.0 (git archive HEAD): dist/index.js = 122706 bytes, dist/index.esm.js = 122244. Working tree: 123360 and 122892 (+654 and +648 bytes). A third build with only the MenuButton helper (lines 42-43) and its three call sites reverted still measured 123075 and 122607 (+369 and +363), so the growth comes from the new off-state reset effect (lines 338-344) plus the MenuButton indirection. Nothing measures it: no .size-limit.json and no test reads dist sizes. Requirement (performance): 'npm run build output for dist/index.js and dist/index.esm.js is no larger than v1.7.0's (measure both before and after)'.
findings.note: Ruled by the arbiter: PERF-001 only requires that the built bundle not grow: I rebuilt the current tree in a scratch copy with the project's own rollup config and measured dist/index.js 122639 and dist/index.esm.js 122171 bytes, both below v1.7.0's 122706/122244, and the PERF-001 test at SidekickMenu.test.tsx:911 already enforces exactly that ceiling. The finding's premise is stale: SidekickMenu.tsx:42 is `const h = React.createElement;` and no MenuButton helper exists (bundle risk also removed), so both its size claim and its 'unproven' claim are contradicted by the code and the measurement.

findings.description: Turning search off clears the query but leaves the stale highlight, so the keyboard highlight silently moves to a different item than the one the user had selected. Dispatch SET_HIGHLIGHTED_INDEX -1 with the term reset so the off-state matches every other term-clearing path.
findings.evidence: The new effect dispatches only SET_SEARCH_TERM. handleSearchChange (lines 283-287) always follows a term change with SET_HIGHLIGHTED_INDEX -1. Scenario: searchEnabled flips true->false while a term is active and an item was arrow-highlighted; the term is dropped but highlightedIndex (e.g. 1) is kept, so after the list unfilters a different item (Banana) is highlighted and Enter activates it, not the item the user had highlighted.

findings.description: The bundle-size guard can pass against a stale dist, so on its own it does not prove the shipped bundle is no larger than v1.7.0's.
